title: Hand-built prototype revived with AI coding (before/after)
author: PieMastaSam
selftext:
Left is a hand-built prototype I started around April last year, before I really knew coding agents were a thing for game work. Took a couple of months to get even that far and yes, I got a bit further than this clip.

I shelved it. I’d seen what AI tools could already do for web, and grinding a game from scratch felt like a waste until those tools matured. Spent about a year getting comfortable with AI coding. Came back, hit the ground running.

Right is where I am now. More progress than the old prototype, in about a quarter of the time. Still glad I learned the basics of game dev first though. I was able to really hit the ground running because I already had a lot of assets I made in blender as well as the core game logic so I could really focus more on having the AI refine what I already had rather than generating everything new from scratch. Been having a an absolute blast working on my old project again! 

Steam (Coming Soon): [https://store.steampowered.com/app/3760350/Astro\_Inc/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3760350/Astro_Inc/) Old DevLogs: [https://www.youtube.com/@SamInDev](https://www.youtube.com/@SamInDev)

Curious what’s working for folks these days... still learning “classic” engines (I’m on Unreal), or more Three.js / web stacks? Don’t see as much Unreal love in the AI clips it seems. Anyone else had decent results seeding AI with old manually made examples?
